text:
Systematic meta-review (Part 1: pharmacological interventions) by Kundakci, Jones, Booth and colleagues for the OPTIC consortium (Critical Care 2025), mapping the meta-analysed evidence for drugs used to prevent or manage delirium in critically ill adults.

SCOPE: The authors searched 8 databases from inception to September 2023 and identified 56 systematic reviews of randomized trials of pharmacological interventions for ICU delirium, of which 17 were mapped in detail with GRADE certainty assessments. Outcomes covered delirium occurrence, duration and severity, ICU and hospital mortality, and length of stay. Up to 7 in 10 ICU patients are expected to develop delirium, with higher rates among mechanically ventilated patients; risk factors include illness severity, older age, pre-existing cognitive impairment, and ICU drugs such as sedatives and analgesics.

KEY FINDINGS: The alpha-2 adrenoceptor agonist drug class (primarily dexmedetomidine) had the largest evidence base and was probably favourable over placebo for preventing or reducing delirium occurrence (moderate- to high-certainty evidence from 2 systematic reviews). It was also probably favourable for reducing ICU and hospital length of stay (moderate certainty). For ICU mortality there may have been little or no difference between dexmedetomidine and non-dexmedetomidine comparators (low certainty), and evidence on hospital mortality was very uncertain. Evidence for other pharmacological comparisons (including antipsychotics) was variable and less certain. No meta-analyses reported outcomes for cognition or emotional distress.

ASSESSMENT: Across the included reviews, delirium was most commonly detected with the Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU), followed by the Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist (ICDSC), the CAM, and DSM criteria. The authors conclude dexmedetomidine-based strategies are the most likely effective pharmacological approach for ICU delirium, while noting gaps in evidence on deprescribing sedatives and on long-term cognitive outcomes. A companion Part 2 covers non-pharmacological and multicomponent interventions.
title: Pharmacological interventions to prevent and manage ICU delirium: a systematic meta-review
